Q1: It means you tried to grant a level the user already holds, or a greater one; grants must raise the level. No remediation is needed because the user already has that access.
Q2: You need model admin access on that model, or controller superuser access.
Q3: Someone with model admin access on the model the offer belongs to, or a controller superuser.
Q4: Revoking the `read` level deletes the permission record outright, since a revoke that takes the level back to `read` is the same write as removing the grant.
Q5: No. Revoking would fail with `user is the last model admin for 1 or more models`; first grant admin on the model to another user.
Q6: Ten level-object combinations are valid. For an offer the valid levels are `read`, `consume` and `admin`.
Q7: It is the greater of the user's own grants and the grants of `everyone@external`, resolved at each access check with nothing stored or cached.
Q8: No. Trying to grant or revoke your own cloud access gives `cannot change your own cloud access`; ask another cloud admin or a controller superuser.
Q9: The pair of object and user: a unique index allows exactly one permission per user per object.
Q10: If the external user is one Juju has not seen yet, the grant creates that user as a side effect, so the record has someone to name.
Q11: No. The access domain exposes no watch surfaces; changes are read on demand, not watched.
Q12: `jaas_access_controller` manages controller access, and it applies when using JAAS.
Q13: The client refuses it with the error `You have specified a controller access permission "<level>"...`; name a model or offer level, or drop the model or offer.
